title: 3. The roadmap is by objective; understanding is by domain

sections.name: observation
sections.label: Observation
sections.content: `clerk roadmap --json` (2026-11-04): period Focus 1, seven objectives, thirteen epics, no domain anywhere. The parent CLAUDE.md still names scripts/roadmap.mjs, which no longer exists. Meanwhile the method layer holds 40 domain records (suggested and affirmed copies), 24 axis-in-domain, 112 poles, 74 tensions, 284 problems, all living flat in Suggestions / Affirmed / Set aside and filtered by type. Nothing joins an epic to a domain, and no view shows one domain whole.

sections.name: owner_picture
sections.label: The owner's picture
sections.content: Web-based generic editor as a domain with its own priorities; within it the essay editor (the first vehicle for local-first, semantic-sovereignty ideas) and the website editor, each with its own personas, problem variants and archetypal lean. Today the nearest records are Evidence-backed writing (the essay domain, five personas-in-domain) and Website copy, which refines Evidence-backed writing and holds one persona (Site author). There is no Web editor parent domain; a parent would hold the general problems (GitHub connection, editor identity) the subdomains assume.

sections.name: inheritance
sections.label: Inheritance
sections.content: Subdomains inherit the parent's axes and poles by default and localise the names; personas come down from the parent but only the primary ones stay relevant. One level down is enough for a view. Today axis-in-domain and persona-in-domain are copied per domain by hand, with refines to the generic tension or persona, so inheritance exists as a convention, not as a rule any tool applies.
